We prove that if $G$ is a $3$-connected graph other than a complete graph or the triangular prism, and $L$ is a list assignment with $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)$ for every vertex $v$, then $G$ has a proper $L$-coloring and any two such colorings can be transformed into one another by a finite sequence of $L$-valid Kempe changes. This proves a conjecture of Chakraborty, Feghali and Mahmoud.
item.dc:creator: Hongyang Wang

item.title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
item.description: arXiv:2610.35708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure atom $A_{\gamma}$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_{\alpha}$, or of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure character $\kappa_{\gamma}$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule. We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_{\lambda}(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_{\gamma}(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Du, Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin

item.title: From skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to sharp Ax-Katz congruences and zero counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.35739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a unified account of zero counting in finite-field polynomial rings with commuting variables twisted by a common automorphism. A decomposition into fixed-field slices connects skew evaluation with ordinary polynomial evaluation. First, we derive a slice coefficient formula from the skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and use it to deduce skew Chevalley-Warning, including the sufficient condition $n>h\sum_i d_i$. Next, classical Ax-Katz gives the corrected integer congruence $Q^{\max\{0,\lceil(n-h\sum_i d_i)/D\rceil\}}\mid N+(M-1)\delta$. We construct homogeneous examples proving optimality for every positive degree table and every number of variables. We also establish a sharp lower bound with a prescribed zero, an input-sensitive coefficient-filtration refinement, and transfers of known bounds for nonlinear zero sets. Detailed calculations explain the origin correction, incomplete norm blocks, and the distinction between characteristic-$p$ summation and higher integer divisibility. Existing geometric, interpolation, and counting theorems are explicitly attributed.
item.dc:creator: Shuang Li, Xuan Pang, Pingzhi Yuan

item.title: Minimum Contagious Sets in Trees with Degree-Proportional Thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how large the minimum size of a contagious set can be among trees of a fixed order. Given a graph $G$ and $\rho\in[0,1]$, an inactive vertex $u$ becomes active when at least $\lceil{\rho d_G(u)\rceil}$ of its neighbors are active. An initial set of active vertices is contagious if the process eventually activates every vertex. We obtain exact values for the minimum size of a contagious set in perfect $d$-ary trees. We then determine the exact maximum of this minimum size over all trees of order $n$. We establish this result by bounding the number of pairwise disjoint resistant sets, each of which must intersect every contagious set, and constructing trees that attain the resulting bounds. Finally, by bounding the change in the minimum size of a contagious set under a leaf exchange, we show that, for $0<\rho\leq1$ and $n\geq2$, every integer between $1$ and this maximum occurs as the minimum size of a contagious set in a tree of order $n$.
item.dc:creator: Jeong-Ok Choi, Collin McDevitt

item.title: P-stable degree sequence regions for bipartite and directed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.35777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The switch Markov chain is a natural method for sampling graph realizations with a prescribed degree sequence, and $P$-stability is a general sufficient condition for its rapid mixing. Since $P$-stability is often difficult to verify directly, we develop an approach based on the simpler and more readily verifiable property of \emph{full graphicality}. We consider bidegree sequence regions obtained by fixing the two class sizes, the common degree sum, and lower and upper bounds for the degrees in each class. Such a region is fully graphic if every bidegree sequence satisfying these constraints has a bipartite realization. Our main result shows that every fully graphic region of this form is $P$-stable. More precisely, for class sizes $n$ and $m$, the perturbation ratio is at most $(nm)^5$. It follows from a known theory that the switch Markov chain is rapidly mixing on every such region. We also show that full graphicality can be tested on a canonical extremal bidegree sequence and use this characterization to derive several new explicit sufficient conditions. By encoding loopless directed graphs as bipartite graphs, we develop a parallel theory for directed degree sequences. This gives analogous extremal characterizations, sufficient conditions for full graphicality, and $P$-stability and rapid-mixing results for directed degree-sequence regions. The encoding process allows most corresponding statements for the two cases to be formulated and proved in one run.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter L. Erd\H{o}s, G\'abor Lippner, Na'ama Nevo, Lajos Soukup

item.title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A permutation $\sigma\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $\sigma(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $\Phi_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $\Phi_p = \Phi_p^{+} \sqcup \Phi_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| \Phi_p^{+} | - | \Phi_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $\sigma\in\Phi_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $\Phi_p^{+}$ versus $\Phi_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $\sigma^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
item.dc:creator: Kian C. Shah, Arthemy V. Kiselev

item.title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $\eta(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Elsholtz

item.title: On the minimality of the compact right-angled 120-cell
item.description: arXiv:2610.33053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a compact right-angled polytope in hyperbolic 4-space has at least 120 facets, with equality only for the right-angled 120-cell. This answers a question of Potyagailo and Vinberg. As a consequence, the right-angled 120-cell is the unique compact right-angled 4-polytope of minimal volume and f-vector.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo, Fangting Zheng

item.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.33131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Nadia S. Larsen, Tron Omland, Henrikke G. Rustad

item.title: Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position
item.description: arXiv:2610.33216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Bolotin, Dmitry Zaporozhets

item.title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.33427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiao Shi, Zeyan Song, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu

item.title: Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and M\'edard in 2009.
item.dc:creator: Kai Cai, Guangyue Han, Mengxi Yang, Wenan Zang

item.title: Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one
item.description: arXiv:2610.33675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation. The coordinate ring of the union of the curves, localized at the chosen points, is essentially of finite type over Q and of dimension at most one. Dropping finiteness costs two conditions, both isolated by Colbert: a poset with no chain of three elements is a Noetherian spectrum exactly when it has finitely many minimal elements and any two distinct ones have finitely many common upper bounds. A variant keeping the shape of the ideals of Alkass but changing their exponents shows why that construction produces only nested neighborhoods. Constraining the ring destroys most of this freedom: normal rings leave finite disjoint unions of stars, domains a single star, local rings a point or a finite co-star. In height two the question is open in general, but the conditions conjectured by Wiegand and Wiegand are not sufficient
item.dc:creator: Xin Li

item.title: On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.33692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.
item.dc:creator: P\'eter P. P\'alfy

item.title: The $\rm{v}$-number of $t$-closed neighborhood ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.33858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$. Lastly, we compute explicit formulas for the $\rm{v}$-number in the case of paths, cycles, and caterpillars, and analyze the case of Hamming graphs.
item.dc:creator: Delio Jaramillo-Velez, Hiram H. L\'opez, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e, Nart Shalqini

item.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.33864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.
item.dc:creator: Yuliy Baryshnikov, Efe Onaran

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.33903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Edison, Alexander Sistko

item.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $\Gamma$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $\Gamma$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $\Gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Feng Deng, Jing Jian Li, Hao Yu

item.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.34160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Liu

item.title: J\'onsson cardinals, Magidor cardinals, and the number of omitted colors
item.description: arXiv:2610.34189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\lambda$ be a Magidor cardinal and let $\alpha\in[\alpha_M,\lambda)$. We show that $\lambda\rightarrow[\lambda]^{\aleph_0-bd}_{\alpha,<\alpha}$. We prove the consistency of a similar statement for J\'onsson cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Shimon Garti

item.title: Asymptotic Rank of Complete Graph Tensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.34273v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph tensors extend the matrix multiplication tensor by placing a two-party identity tensor on every edge of a graph and keeping one tensor leg at every vertex. We study the asymptotic rank of the tensor associated with the complete graph. For every integer $n\geq 2$, over the complex numbers, we prove \[ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor \leq \log_2\widetilde R\bigl(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)\bigr) \leq \frac{n^2}{4}. \] The upper bound matches the maximum-cut lower bound for every even $n$ and differs from it by only $1/4$ for every odd $n$. In particular, the exponent per edge is below $2/3$ for every $n\geq5$, answering a question of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. Our proof extends the polynomial multiplication approach underlying OpenAI's bound $\omega\leq9/4$. The main step separates any fixed number of shared tensor legs simultaneously, using only linearly many direct-sum copies in the number of blocks. This yields an entropy inequality for higher-order tensors. We apply it to the tensor for multiplying $n-1$ polynomials, whose rank is linear in the input length. Discrete concavity and a shifted tripling inequality then force a lower bound on a symmetrized spectral profile. Comparing this growth with polynomial interpolation gives the stated upper bound while preserving all $n$ tensor legs. We also prove an operational barrier for these higher-order polynomial constructions. For $n\geq3$, the specified formal reduction rules cannot certify an exponent below $n^2/4$ for $\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)$, even after taking tensor powers and allowing subexponential overhead and common auxiliary factors. This extends the symmetric three-leg barrier of Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam and explains the remaining gap for odd complete graphs within this method.
item.dc:creator: Huanyi Zhou

item.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.34288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Characterization Problem asks whether a finite abelian group with Davenport constant at least four is determined, up to isomorphism, by its system of length sets. This is a central inverse problem in non-unique factorization theory: it asks whether the possible numbers of irreducible factors retain enough information to recover the underlying class group. For rings of integers of algebraic number fields, an affirmative answer means that the ideal class group can be recovered from these factorization lengths alone. We resolve this problem for all homocyclic groups $C_n^r$: if $G$ is a finite abelian group with $\mathsf D(G)\ge4$ and $\mathcal L(G)=\mathcal L(C_n^r)$, then $G\cong C_n^r$. The cross number of a sequence is the sum of the reciprocals of the orders of its terms. This weighted measure of sequence length links zero-sum theory with half-factoriality, and determining its maximal value for minimal zero-sum sequences is a longstanding extremal problem. We also obtain an exact formula for the maximal cross number of minimal zero-sum sequences over subsets whose minimum distance is divisible by the rank of the ambient group minus one. For $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ and $r\ge\max\{2,n_r-2\}$, we prove \[ \mathsf K(G,r-1)=1+(r-1)\sum_{p\mid n_1} \left(1-p^{-\mathsf v_p(n_1)}\right), \] which is a key ingredient in resolving the Characterization Problem for homocyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Qinghai Zhong

item.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
item.description: arXiv:2610.34300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: Optimal solution ranks in the Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every $n$ and $r$ with $1\le r$ and $\binom{r+1}{2}\le n$, we construct a connected unweighted graph on $n$ vertices whose Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation has a unique optimal solution of rank $r$. The main examples are the Kneser graphs $K(m,2)$, whose unique optima have rank $m-1$. A six-vertex wheel supplies rank three, and attaching pendant vertices preserves both rank and uniqueness. For dense random graphs, we also prove a polynomial lower bound on the optimal rank.
item.dc:creator: Avinash Bhardwaj, Vishnu Narayanan

item.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.
item.dc:creator: Martin Anthony

item.title: Online Discrepancy of Sparse Random Vectors over Long Horizons
item.description: arXiv:2610.34410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=\Theta(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time. Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $\Omega(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{\alpha_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $\alpha_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$. The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Envy-Free Allocations for Random Non-Additive Valuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benade et al. (EC 2024) introduced a semi-random model for non-additive fair division in which each agent starts with an arbitrary base valuation over bundles of items and independently permutes the item names uniformly at random. While they proved that envy-free allocations exist with high probability as the number of items grows for $n = 2$ agents, they left open whether the same holds for $n > 2$ agents. We resolve this open question in the affirmative: for any fixed number of agents $n$ and any number of items $m$ divisible by $n$, an envy-free allocation exists with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $m \to \infty$. Our proof combines the second moment method with a connection to the (small-set) expansion of generalized Johnson graphs, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Pasin Manurangsi

item.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34482v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/\pi^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Ap\'ery-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.
item.dc:creator: Noam Shalev

item.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
item.description: arXiv:2610.34530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Bufetov, Yuan Tian

item.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.
item.dc:creator: June Huh, Mateusz Micha{\l}ek, Botong Wang, Jian Xiao

item.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Dung The Tran, Boqing Xue

item.title: Exponentially large mu-coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carotenuto, Christophe Hohlweg, Paolo Papi

item.title: Falconer estimate for circular and cinematic Furstenberg problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.35213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Falconer-type bound $\dim_{\mathrm H}F\geq u+1$ for planar circular $(u,v)$-Furstenberg sets whenever $0<u\leq1$, $0<v\leq3$, and $2u+v\geq3$. The same bound holds for smooth cinematic curve families. This resolves the circular Furstenberg conjecture of Green, Harris, Ou, Ren, and Tammen in its full Falconer range $2u+v\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Xie

item.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2610.35292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $\alpha$, let $\lambda_{k,\alpha}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24\lambda_{k,\alpha}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^\alpha}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^\alpha n+\lambda_{k,\alpha}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(\alpha+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Maity, Manjil P. Saikia, Prabal Talukdar

item.title: Antimagic Labeling of Central Digraphs Constructed from Loops
item.description: arXiv:2610.35419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(T, \circ)$ be a loop of order $k \geq 3$ and $D_S^*$ the loopless central digraph obtained from the associated central digraph $D_S$ by removing the $k$ self-loops at the diagonal vertices. We construct an explicit arc-labeling $f$ of $D_S^*$ ordering all arcs lexicographically by $(\text{tail}, \text{head})$ and assigning labels $1, \ldots, m$ in that order and prove that $f$ is an antimagic labeling. Consequently, $D_S$ is antimagic for every loop of order $k \geq 3$, a property that depends only on $k$ and is invariant across all non-isomorphic loops of the same order.
item.dc:creator: Raja Rawat

item.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.35783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Tur\'an expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.
item.dc:creator: Wenle Shi

item.title: Computational complexity of the $H$-coloring problem in cubic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.35794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: If $G$ and $H$ are two cubic graphs, then an $H$-coloring of $G$ is a mapping $f: E(G)\rightarrow E(H)$, such that for every $v\in V(G)$ there is a vertex $x\in V(H)$, such that $f(\partial_G(v))=\partial_H(x)$. If $G$ admits an $H$-coloring then it is common to write $H\prec G$. In this paper, for a fixed connected cubic graph $H$, we consider a decision problem, which we call $H$-coloring. In this problem, on the input one is given a connected cubic graph $G$. The goal is to decide whether $H\prec G$. A conjecture by Hakobyan and the author states that $H$-coloring is polynomial time solvable, if $H$ does not admit a $P_{12}$-coloring. Here $P_{12}$ is the unique cubic graph obtained from the Petersen graph by expanding one of its vertices into a triangle. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture under $P\neq NP$, by showing that $S_6$-coloring is NP-complete. Here $S_6$ is the unique cubic graph on six vertices having exactly one bridge. Our second result is an algorithm that solves $H$-coloring problem in time $O^*(c^n)$, where $H$ is a simple connected cubic graph, $n$ is the number of vertices of the input cubic graph $G$ and $c=\sqrt{8}\approx 2.8284$.
item.dc:creator: Vahan Mkrtchyan

item.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.
item.dc:creator: Nina Zubrilina

item.title: Bootstrap percolation and $P_3$-hull number in direct products of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2403.10957v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation is a graph infection process based on the update rule by which a vertex with $r$ infected neighbors becomes infected. We say that an initial set of infected vertices propagates if all vertices of a graph $G$ are eventually infected, and the minimum cardinality of such a set in $G$ is called the $r$-bootstrap percolation number, $m(G,r)$, of $G$. In this paper, we study percolating sets in direct products of graphs. While in general graphs there is no non-trivial upper bound on $m(G\times H,r)$, we prove several upper bounds under the assumption $\delta(G)\ge r$. We also characterize the connected graphs $G$ and $H$ with minimum degree $2$ that satisfy $m(G \times H, 2) = \frac{|V(G \times H)|}{2}$. In addition, we determine the exact values of $m(P_n \times P_m, 2)$, which are $m+n$ if $m$ and $n$ are both even, and $m+n-1$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Bo\v{s}tjan Bre\v{s}ar, Jaka Hed\v{z}et, Rebekah Herrman

item.title: Density Hajnal--Szemer\'{e}di theorem for cliques of size four
item.description: arXiv:2501.00801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The exact minimum-degree thresholds that guarantee the existence of $k$ vertex-disjoint copies of the complete graph $K_r$ in an $n$-vertex graph were determined in the celebrated theorems of Dirac (1952) for $r=2$, Corr\'adi--Hajnal (1963) for $r=3$, and Hajnal--Szemer\'edi (1970) for general $r \ge 4$. A natural and fundamental problem is to determine the corresponding average-degree (or density) thresholds. This problem turns out to be substantially more difficult. The seminal theorem of Erd\H{o}s--Gallai (1959) resolved the case $r=2$. The case $r=3$ was settled for large $n$ by Allen, B\"ottcher, Hladk\'y, and Piguet~\cite{ABHP15}, who remarkably identified four distinct classes of extremal constructions arising in different ranges of $k$. They further posed the problem of establishing a density analogue of the Hajnal--Szemer\'edi theorem, noting that ``We are not even sure what the complete family of extremal graphs should be.'' In this paper, we establish an asymptotic density Hajnal-Szemer\H{e}di theorem for \(K_4\) by determining \(\mathrm{ex}(n,(k+1)K_4)\) up to an additive \(O(n)\) term for all integers \(n\ge 4k\ge 0\). Five families of constructions show that this bound is sharp up to an additive \(O(n)\) term. For general \(r\ge 5\), we propose a candidate family consisting of \(r+1\) extremal construction classes.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Hou, Caiyun Hu, Xizhi Liu, Yixiao Zhang

item.title: Embedding edge-colored graphs in expanders with roll-back
item.description: arXiv:2501.14286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a method to embed edge-colored graphs into families of expander graphs, which generalizes a framework developed by Dragani\'c, Krivelevich, and Nenadov (2022). As an application, we show that each family of sufficiently pseudo-random graphs on $n$ vertices contains every edge-colored subdivision of $K_\Delta$, provided that the distance between branch vertices in the subdivision is large enough, the average degree of each graph in the family is at least $(1+o(1))\Delta$, and the number of vertices in the subdivision is at most $(1-o(1))n$. This extends the subdivision-embedding results of Dragani\'c, Krivelevich, and Nenadov to the colorful setting. Even in the monochromatic case, our work extends the earlier result, which only applied to graphs with average degree at most $O(n^{1/5})$. This work is motivated in part by the problem of finding structures in distance graphs defined over finite vector spaces. In particular, we obtain nearly spanning subdivisions of complete graphs with arbitrary prescribed nonzero edge distances in sufficiently large subsets of these spaces.
item.dc:creator: Ben Lund, Chuandong Xu

item.title: Identically vanishing $k$-generalized Fibonacci polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2507.11596v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recurrence for the $k$-Fibonacci polynomials is usually iterated upwards to positive values of $n$ only. When the recurrence is iterated downwards to $n<0$, there are indices where the polynomials vanish identically. This fact does not seem to have been noted in the literature. We derive the set of such indices. We establish the connection of our results to the solution of the Skolem problem for the $k$-Fibonacci numbers. For $k\ge3$ and $n<0$, we show that the degree of the polynomial does not increase monotonically with $|n|$. The so-called `left-justified $k$-nomial triangle' is extended to treat negative indices. We derive expressions for the individual polynomial coefficients (the elementary symmetric polynomials of the roots). We present results for the properties of the polynomials, for both $n>0$ and $n<0$, including factorization of the polynomials and properties of the roots. Results are also derived for real roots. We present new, tighter, bounds on the amplitudes of the nonzero roots. We derive new combinatorial sums for the polynomial coefficients, which are more concise and computationally efficient than previously published expressions.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Mane

item.title: Comparing classes of highly symmetric graphs: From $2$-arc-transitive to $2$-distance-transitive
item.description: arXiv:2508.02010v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $2$-distance-transitive graph is a vertex-transitive graph whose vertex stabilizer is transitive on both the first- and second-step neighborhoods. This concept simultaneously generalizes both distance-transitive graphs and $2$-arc-transitive graphs. In this paper, we first determine the vertex-quasiprimitive types of $2$-distance-transitive graphs of odd order, partially answering a question posed by A. Devillers, M. Giudici, C. H. Li and C. E. Praeger in 2012. We then prove that a $2$-distance-transitive graph of valency $p+1$, where $p$ is a prime, is $2$-arc-transitive if and only if it has girth at least $4$. We also show that every locally-primitive $2$-distance-transitive graph of valency at most $8$ is $2$-arc-transitive, with the icosahedron as the unique exception. Finally, we prove that if $\Gamma$ is a $G$-locally-primitive, $(G,2)$-distance-transitive graph of valency at least $3$ and $G$ is soluble, then either $\Gamma\cong \K_{p,p}$ for some prime $p$, or the order of $\Gamma$ is not square-free.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jin, Jack H. Koolen, Chenhui Lv

item.title: The spectral Tur\'{a}n problem: Characterizing spectral-consistent graphs
item.description: arXiv:2508.12070v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let ${\rm EX}(n,H)$ and ${\rm SPEX}(n,H)$ denote the families of $H$-free graphs of order $n$ with maximum size and maximum spectral radius, respectively. A graph $H$ is called spectral-consistent if ${\rm SPEX}(n,H)\subseteq {\rm EX}(n,H)$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$. Cioab\u{a}, Desai, and Tait put forward the following conjecture: Let $H$ be a graph for which every graph in ${\rm EX}(n,H)$ is a Tur\'{a}n graph plus $O(1)$ edges. Then $H$ is spectral-consistent. Wang, Kang, and Xue settled this conjecture. Recently, Liu and Ning raised a general problem in spectral extremal graph theory: Characterize all graphs that are spectral-consistent. In this paper, we establish that for any finite graph $H$, if its decomposition family is matching-good, then $H$ is necessarily spectral-consistent. Notably, this structural condition is strictly weaker than the condition for spectral-consistency established by Wang, Kang, and Xue in their earlier work, thereby broadening the class of graphs known to satisfy the spectral-consistency property. Our main result enables us to fully characterize spectral consistency for several important families of forbidden graphs $H$, including generalized color-critical graphs, odd-balloonings of nontrivial trees and complete bipartite graphs $K_{s,t}$ with $t\geq s\geq 2$ and $(s,t)\neq(2,3)$, as well as edge blow-ups of non-bipartite graphs and even cycles. Furthermore, we present a streamlined proof of the Chen--Lei--Li theorem on the spectral-consistency of disjoint unions of suspensions of unions of color-critical graphs. Finally, we propose an open problem to motivate future research in this area.
item.dc:creator: Longfei Fang, Sergey Goryainov, Denis Krotov, Huiqiu Lin, Mingqing Zhai

item.title: Global coalitions in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.15386v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G=(V, E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ is called a global dominating set of $G$ if it is a dominating set of both $G$ and its complement $\overline{G}$. Two disjoint subsets $V_1, V_2 \subseteq V$ form a global coalition if neither $V_1$ nor $V_2$ is a global dominating set, but their union $V_1 \cup V_2$ is. A global coalition partition (abbreviated $gc$-partition) of $G$ is a vertex partition $\pi$ of $V(G)$ such that every class of $\pi$ forms a global coalition with some other class of $\pi$. The global coalition number $GC(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a $gc$-partition of $G$. In this paper, we initiate the study of these concepts. We prove that every graph of order at least two admits a $gc$-partition, give general lower bounds on $GC(G)$, and bound the number of global coalitions in which a single class of a $gc$-partition can be involved. We show that $GC(G)$ coincides with the coalition number $C(G)$ whenever $G$ is disconnected or has radius at least three, and consequently that $GC(G)=C(\overline{G})$ for every join of two graphs. We determine the global coalition number of complete multipartite graphs with at most three parts, wheels, fans, paths, cycles and trees of radius two, characterise the graphs $G$ with $GC(G)=|V(G)|$ in terms of antitwins, relate global coalitions to perfect coalitions, and study unicyclic graphs of radius at most two. Finally, we interpret $gc$-partitions in the language of fair division of indivisible goods and pose several open problems.\\ \textbf{2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:} 05C69, 91B32.\\ \textbf{JEL Classification:} C72, C78, D63.\\ \textbf{Keywords}: Global domination, coalition, global coalition partition, antitwins, trees, unicyclic graphs, fair division.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Anholcer, Nazli Besharati, Doost Ali Mojdeh, Mohammad Reza Samadzadeh

item.title: Line-width and path-width
item.description: arXiv:2509.16786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For finite graphs, path-width is an interesting and useful concept, but if we extend it to infinite graphs in the most obvious way (by making the indexing path infinite), it does not work nicely. The simplest extension that works nicely is to allow the indexing set to be any totally-ordered set, and then the corresponding decomposition is called a ``line-decomposition'', and the maximum bag size needed is called ``line-width''. In particular, the indexing set need not be a well-order; but the corresponding decomposition would be easier to use if it was. We show that if a graph has line-width at most $k$, it admits a well-ordered line-decomposition with width at most $2k$, and this is best possible.
item.dc:creator: Tung Nguyen, Alex Scott, Paul Seymour

item.title: Leaky Zero Forcing on Subgraphs of $d$-dimensional Grid Graphs with an Application to Diamond Rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2509.21529v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study zero forcing and $\ell$-leaky zero forcing on Diamond rectangle graphs $DR(a,b)$, a family of induced subgraphs of 2-dimensional grid graphs. Motivated by this family, we develop more general results for subgraphs of $d$-dimensional grid graphs. Using $\ell$-leaky forts, we show that for $\ell\leq 2d-1$, every nonempty $\ell$-leaky fort in a subgraph of $P_{n_1}\square\cdots\square P_{n_d}$ must contain a vertex of degree at most $2d-1$. This gives bounds and, in certain cases, exact values for the $\ell$-leaky forcing number of such subgraphs. We then apply these results to Diamond rectangle graphs, for which we show that the zero forcing number equals the maximum nullity and completely characterize the $\ell$-leaky forcing number for all $\ell\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Moruzzi Jr, Sagar Shah, Aaditeya Tripathi

item.title: Online Ramsey numbers of the claw versus cycles
item.description: arXiv:2601.05452v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The online Ramsey number $\tilde r(G,H)$ is defined via a Builder--Painter game on an empty graph with countably many vertices. In each round, Builder reveals an edge, which Painter immediately colors either red or blue. Builder wins once a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ appears, and $\tilde r(G,H)$ is the minimum number of edges Builder must reveal to force a win. For a long cycle $C_\ell$, the online Ramsey numbers $\tilde r(G,C_\ell)$ are known only for a few specific choices of $G$. In particular, exact values were determined for $G=P_3$ by Cyman, Dzido, Lapinskas, and Lo (Electron. J. Combin., 2015), while asymptotically tight results were obtained when $G$ is an even cycle by Adamski, Bednarska-Bzd\c{e}ga, and Bla\v{z}ej (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2024). In this paper, we consider the case where $G$ is the claw $K_{1,3}$ and determine the exact value of $\tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)$. We show that \[ \tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)=\left\lfloor \frac{3(\ell+1)}{2} \right\rfloor \quad \text{for all } \ell \ge 13. \]
item.dc:creator: Hexuan Zhi, Yanbo Zhang

item.title: Coloopless zonotopes and counterexamples to the Shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2603.24784v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Henze and Malikiosis (2017) have shown that the Lonely Runner Conjecture (LRC) can be restated as a convex-geometric question on the so-called LR zonotopes, lattice zonotopes with one more generator than their dimension. This relation naturally suggests a more general statement, the shifted LRC, the zonotopal version of which concerns a classical parameter, the covering radius. In this paper we do two things: 1) We show explicit counterexamples to both the shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture (starting at $n=5$) and to the Lonely Vector Property of Malikiosis-Schymura-Santos (2025). 2) We push the analogies between the two versions of LRC and their zonotopal counterparts, in particular highlighting that the proofs of the finite-checking Theorems A and B in Malikiosis-Schymura-Santos (2025) are more transparent, and the statements more general, if regarded in terms of two quite general classes of lattice zonotopes: the coloopless zonotopes that we introduce here and the cosimple ones, already defined by them.
item.dc:creator: M\'onica Blanco, Francisco Criado, Francisco Santos

item.title: Enumerations and Bijections for Stanley Polyominoes
item.description: arXiv:2604.12392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stanley polyominoes are a subclass of parallelogram polyominoes in which each row begins strictly to the right of the beginning of the previous row and ends strictly to the right of the end of the previous row. In this paper, we derive generating functions for Stanley polyominoes with respect to the numbers of columns and rows, area, semiperimeter, and numbers of interior points and edges. We also establish combinatorial connections through bijections with other combinatorial structures such as Dyck paths, skew Ferrers diagrams, and peakless Motzkin paths. As a byproduct, we answer the open question of finding a bijection between parallelogram polyominoes of area $n$ with $k$ columns and coin fountains with $n$ coins in the odd-numbered rows and $n-k$ coins in the even-numbered rows.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Baril, Aubrey Blecher, Jos\'e Luis ram\'irez

item.title: On separability of Tatra association schemes
item.description: arXiv:2605.07672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Tatra association scheme is an association scheme arising from a symmetric bilinear form defined on the equivalence classes of nonzero $2$-dimensional vectors modulo some subgroup of the multiplicative group of a finite field. In the present paper, we prove that every such association scheme is $4$-separable, i.e., it is determined up to isomorphism by the tensor of its $4$-dimensional intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Grigory Ryabov

item.title: Improved bounds on the b-chromatic number using the independence and chromatic numbers
item.description: arXiv:2606.07461v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finding a minimum proper vertex coloring is $\NP$-hard and hard to approximate. $B$-coloring is used as a heuristic approach to graph coloring. A b-coloring of a graph $G$ is a proper vertex coloring where each color class contains at least one vertex (a b-vertex) adjacent to a vertex in every other color class. The maximum number of colors in such a coloring is the b-chromatic number, ${\rm b}(G)$. A ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring is a variation in which a b-vertex is adjacent to a b-vertex in every other color class. We employ the ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring to prove that any $n$-vertex graph $G$ with independence number at most $t$ satisfies ${\rm b}(G) \leq [(t-1)n+t\chi(G)]/(2t-1)$. This bound extends the bounds of Kouider and Zaker (2006) and Alkhateeb and Kohl (2011) and significantly improves the bound in terms of the clique partition number. We show that this bound is sharp for all $t\geq 2$ and $\chi(G)\geq 3$. Furthermore, we provide a refined bound based on the maximum number of vertex-disjoint independent sets of size $t$. Finally, we prove ${\rm b}^{\ast}(G) \leq [(t-2)n+(t-1)\chi(G)]/(2t-3)$ for all $K_{1,t}$-free graphs $G$, a significant improvement over the analogous bound for ${\rm b}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Manouchehr Zaker

item.title: $C$-networks and the planar Ising inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.15082v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the inverse problem for Ising models on reduced planar graphs in a disk, i.e., recovering the edge coupling constants from the boundary spin correlations. A recursive solution to this problem was provided by Galashin--Pylyavskyy. Our solution is nonrecursive. It is based on an Ising analog of the chamber ansatz which asserts that the inverse map factors through variables on the graph that transform under the Ising Y-$\Delta$ move according to the discrete CKP equation.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Elmaazouz, Terrence George

item.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
item.description: arXiv:2606.18048v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that any $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)\Big(\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target for the constant, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also arises independently as the shattering threshold for coloring and finding large independent sets in sparse random hypergraphs. We show that uncrowded hypergraphs attain this threshold: for $k \ge 2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies $$\chi_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ This matches the coupon-collector heuristic, and establishes a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. As a consequence, we show that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $c_k\Big(\frac{\Delta}{\log \Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ with $c_k=1-o_k(1)$, resolving, in a stronger form, a recent conjecture of Verstra\"ete and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs. Our techniques yield the first palette sparsification result for hypergraph coloring using $o(\Delta^{\frac{1}{k-1}})$ colors per vertex. Specifically, for an uncrowded $k$-graph $\mathcal{H}$ and $q=\Theta\Big({\Big(\frac{\Delta}{\gamma\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}}\Big)$, sampling $\Theta(\Delta^{\frac{\gamma}{k-1}})$ colors per vertex suffices to obtain a proper $q$-coloring of $\mathcal{H}$ w.h.p. As an algorithmic consequence, we obtain a single-pass streaming algorithm using $O\big(n^{1+o(1)}\big)$ space for uncrowded $k$-graphs, and, via hypergraph partitioning, for linear hypergraphs as well.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo

item.title: Strong counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture in every uniformity
item.description: arXiv:2606.26735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The supersaturation problem asks, for a fixed $r$-graph $\mathcal F$, for the minimum number of copies of $\mathcal F$ in an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal F)+q$ edges. Mubayi conjectured a local form of supersaturation under a stability hypothesis: if $\mathcal F$ is non-$r$-partite and stable, meaning roughly that the extremal $\mathcal F$-free construction is unique and all near-extremal $\mathcal F$-free $r$-graphs are close to it, then this minimum should be at least $q c(n,\mathcal F)$, where $c(n,\mathcal F)$ is the minimum number of copies created by adding one edge to the extremal $\mathcal F$-free $r$-graph. We disprove this conjectured local lower bound in the strongest possible quantitative sense that the ratio to the conjectured lower bound can be made arbitrarily small. More precisely, for every $r\ge2$ and every $K>1$, we construct a stable non-$r$-partite $r$-graph $\mathcal F$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every $1\le q\le\delta n$, there is an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal F)+q$ edges containing at most $K^{-1}q c(n,\mathcal F)$ copies of $\mathcal F$. This arbitrarily large failure already occurs when $q=1$.
item.dc:creator: Heng Li, Hong Liu, Xizhi Liu, Jing Wang

item.title: Polynomiality of Stretched Schubert Structure Constants and Key Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2607.18746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that monomial coefficients in affine families of key and Schubert polynomials are eventually polynomial. These results extend to finite products. Using M.~Watanabe's Schubert duality, we deduce that stretched Schubert structure constants are eventually polynomial. This proves a conjecture stated by I.~Pak and Z.~Slonim. We also prove that the positive key expansion of every affine-code family of Schubert polynomials eventually has fixed coefficients and affine indices. The proofs combine Demazure operators and vector partition functions with P.~Magyar's orthodontic formula and the generalized Demazure character theory of V.~Lakshmibai, P.~Littelmann, and P.~Magyar.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson

item.title: A complete solution to the Boots-Royle/Cao-Vince conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2607.19268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Boots and Royle, and independently Cao and Vince, conjectured that the join of an edge and a path on $n-2$ vertices is the unique planar graph of maximum adjacency spectral radius for $n\geq 9$. Tait and Tobin (JCTB, 2017) proved the conjecture for sufficiently large order. In this paper, we completely resolved the Boots-Royle/Cao-Vince conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Lele Liu, Bo Ning, Yi Wang

item.title: Bounds on Odd and Odd-Even Induced Subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.02339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph and let $\ell:V(G)\to\mathbb{F}_2$ prescribe degree parities. A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is $\ell$-admissible if every $v\in S$ has degree congruent to $\ell(v)$ modulo $2$ in $G[S]$. Let $h_\ell(G)$ be the maximum order of an $\ell$-admissible set, set $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G):=\min_\ell h_\ell(G)$, and write $f_o(G):=h_{\mathbf{1}}(G)$, where $\mathbf{1}(v)=1$ for every $v\in V(G).$ We prove three main results for graphs without isolated vertices. First, by extending Zeng's odd-cut method to arbitrary parity prescriptions and introducing a one-sided completion lemma, we show that $h_\ell(G)\ge 2n/11$ for every $\ell$. Consequently, $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G)\ge 2n/11$, improving the previous bound $2n/21$. Second, for bipartite graphs we derive lower bounds on $f_o(G)$ in terms of the $\mathbb{F}_2$-rank of the bipartite adjacency matrix and combine them to obtain \[ f_o(G)\ge \left(\frac14+\frac1{256}\right)n=\frac{65}{256}n. \] Thus, in the bipartite case, the factor $2$ in Scott's bound $f_o(G)\ge n/(2\chi(G))$ can be replaced by $128/65<2$. Finally, a fourth-moment argument gives, for $\alpha=\alpha(G)\ge2$ and $\delta(G)\ge 1$, \[ f_o(G)\ge \frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\log_3\alpha}{8} -\frac14\log_3\log_3\sqrt{\alpha}. \] We also construct bipartite graphs satisfying \[ f_o(G)\le \frac{\alpha(G)}2+\log_2\!\bigl(\alpha(G)+1\bigr)+\frac12, \] showing that the logarithmic additive improvement over Scott's bound $f_o(G)\ge\alpha(G)/2$ has the optimal order of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Qiwen Guo, Gregory Gutin, Yiming Hao, Yongtang Shi, Yong Zhang, Yacong Zhou

item.title: On graphs without cycles of length $0$ modulo $3$ or $4$ modulo $6$
item.description: arXiv:2608.06698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study graphs containing no cycle whose length is divisible by $3$ or congruent to $4$ modulo $6$. We prove that every such $n$-vertex graph $G$, where $n \ge 2$, satisfies $e(G) \le (11/8)n-7/4$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $n=8k+2$ for some nonnegative integer $k$ and $G$ is isomorphic to the explicitly constructed graph $H_k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq2$, an $n$-vertex graph with $\left\lfloor (11/8)n-7/4 \right\rfloor$ edges satisfying the same cycle restriction. Consequently, this is the exact maximum number of edges for every $n \ge 2$.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Ueoro

item.title: Farey Structure in Modulo Krinkle Tilings: Mediant Splicing and Generation of Prototiles from a Single Edge
item.description: arXiv:2609.01270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Modulo Krinkle tilings of Imura (arXiv:2506.07638) form a family of non-periodic, spiral monohedral tilings parametrized by a reduced fraction $m/k$ and an integer $t\ge 2$. We show that the Farey sum (mediant) $(m_1+m_2)/(k_1+k_2)$ of two Farey-adjacent parameters is realized by an exact geometric operation on prototiles: the lower boundary path of the $(m_1+m_2,k_1+k_2)$-prototile is obtained by concatenating the parents' lower paths after an edge-length-preserving progressive rotation (fan-twist) of their edges. Conversely, every prototile admits exactly one fan-twist splice decomposition -- no non-adjacent parameters ever splice -- the cut position being $k_1=m^{-1}\bmod k$, and the recursion descends the Stern-Brocot tree to a single unit edge. The combinatorial core of the operation is the classical standard factorization of Christoffel words; the contribution here is its exact edge-isometric realization on circular direction systems and the resulting structure theory for the Modulo Krinkle family, including the recently introduced variants: we prove a separation theorem stating that every variant prototile is the common recursively-generated core plus finitely many direction-invariant decoration edges. As a corollary of Imura's spiral-arm count formula, the two Farey parents are visible in the offset-free tiling itself: the numbers of counterclockwise and clockwise spiral arms are $tk_1$ and $tk_2$.
item.dc:creator: Mikihiro Fujiwara

item.title: Induced Size-Ramsey Numbers of Odd Cycles via Spread Measures
item.description: arXiv:2609.06481v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for every $k\ge2$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, the induced size--Ramsey number of $C_n$ satisfies \[ \widehat R_{\mathrm{ind}}(C_n;k)=e^{\Theta(k)}n. \] This improves the previous upper bound of $e^{O(k\log k)}n$ and resolves a conjecture of Brada\v{c}, Dragani\'c and Sudakov. We obtain this result by proving a stronger form of their odd-hole gadget conjecture: we construct a graph with $e^{O(k)}$ edges whose every $k$-edge-colouring contains a monochromatic induced odd cycle of length $O(\log k)$. Our proof develops a spread-based approach to finding induced cycles. The key idea is to place spread probability weights directly on families of candidate cycles and control their possible chords through a quadratic chord score. Combining this with random sparsification and hypergraph containers yields a sparse host graph that works for every $k$-edge-colouring.
item.dc:creator: Lanchao Wang, Xiaolin Wang

item.title: Real-rooted Eulerian polynomials from permutations, words, and paths
item.description: arXiv:2609.07325v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study seven Eulerian-type polynomial families. We prove that the descent polynomials of derangements are real-rooted, settling the derangement part of a conjecture of S.~Fu, Z.~Lin, and J.~Zeng. We also resolve the real-rootedness conjecture in OEIS A335340, strengthen the known rowwise real-rootedness of an even-top descent family to consecutive strict interlacing, and prove real-rootedness, consecutive interlacing, and real-rooted gamma-polynomials for U.~Shankar's super-Eulerian polynomials. A differential recurrence gives consecutive weak interlacing for ternary words counted by increasing runs. We prove stability of the peak-value refinement and consecutive interleaving of its positive weighted diagonals, settling a conjecture of P.~Alexandersson and O.~Nabawanda. Finally, we prove that the zig-zag Eulerian polynomials, which enumerate swaps in alternating permutations, have simple negative roots, settling the real-rootedness conjecture of T.~Kyle Petersen and Y.~Zhuang.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson

item.title: Matchings and shape-Wilf-Equivalence of sets of patterns of length three I: Triples
item.description: arXiv:2609.08562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Permutation pattern avoidance on Ferrers boards has become a central topic in enumerative combinatorics with important connections to matchings, set partitions, and other combinatorial structures as it allows one to build families of Wilf-equivalent patterns. While shape-Wilf-equivalence classes have been completely determined for individual patterns and pairs of patterns of length three, the corresponding classification for larger pattern sets has remained open. In this paper, we provide a complete classification of the shape-Wilf-equivalence classes of triples of patterns of length three. Our proofs use a bijective encoding of pattern avoiding transversals to establish all equivalence classes. As an application, we enumerate matchings avoiding triples of patterns of length three for all, extending previous results of Bloom and Elizalde. These enumerative results identify additional families of combinatorial objects counted by the Fuss-Catalan numbers and by other integer sequences appearing in the OEIS.
item.dc:creator: Sucharita Biswas, Umesh Shankar, Sivaramakrishnan Sivasubramanian

item.title: The maximum spectral radius of outerplanar and planar $k$-uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.10660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $k\ge3$, a $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected outerplane graph whose interior faces are bounded by $k$-cycles, and a closed $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected plane graph all of whose faces are bounded by $k$-cycles. Their face hypergraphs have the same vertices as the graphs; the hyperedges are the vertex sets of the interior faces, respectively all faces. For $k=3$, the extremal problems over these hypergraphs agree with those for the outerplanar and planar $3$-uniform hypergraphs of Ellingham, Lu and Wang, who determined the outerplanar maximizer for large $n$ and conjectured the planar one. In this paper, for each fixed $k$, we determine the hypergraphs of maximum spectral radius in both classes for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the corresponding face-count divisibility condition. In the outerplanar case, the unique extremal hypergraph is the face hypergraph of the fan, in which one vertex lies on every interior face. In the planar case with $k=3$, it is the face hypergraph of $K_2+P_{n-2}$, which confirms the conjecture of Ellingham, Lu and Wang. For $k\ge4$, the extremal hypergraphs are the face hypergraphs of balanced theta graphs, in which two vertices lie on every face. For $k=4$, the result holds for every $n\ge5$, with extremal hypergraph ${\mathcal H}(K_{2,n-2})$. For $k\ge6$ and an even number of faces, there are exactly $\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor$ extremal hypergraphs up to isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Pei Liu, Suil O

item.title: Proper circular arc graphs are $e$-positive
item.description: arXiv:2609.33124v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an $e$-positive formula for the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs solving the $q=1$ case of a conjecture of Ellzey and of Alexandersson and Panova. In doing so, we provide a new proof of the $e$-positivity of unit interval graphs, which alongside Guay-Paquet's reduction gives a new proof of the Stanley--Stembridge conjecture. We define color matrices, which count proper colorings, and tableau matrices, whose entries are nonnegative rational numbers and ratios of elementary symmetric functions. We prove the two matrices are related by a single family of change of basis matrices, which become invertible after restricting to finitely many colors, and we show the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs comes from taking the trace of these matrices. Using Hikita's tableaux, this gives an explicit formula for the chromatic symmetric function of a proper circular arc graph as a weighted sum over tableaux whose first and last $k$ vertices lie in the same columns.
item.dc:creator: Aarush Vailaya

item.title: Intersecting integer partitions: star bounds and counterexamples at every scale
item.description: arXiv:2610.01747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two integer partitions $t$-intersect if they have at least $t$ common parts, counted with multiplicity. We study the largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ positive parts. The canonical $t$-star consists of the partitions containing at least $t$ ones. Applying Kupavskii's weak-spread theorem, we prove that this star is largest whenever $n\ge Ak^3$, for every fixed $A>24$ and all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly over $1\le t<k$. We also give counterexamples to Borg's conjecture at every intersection scale: for all sufficiently large $k$ and for every $1\le t\le \lceil k/4\rceil$, we describe $t$-intersecting families on integer partitions of $n=\lfloor tk^2/3\rfloor$ into $k$ parts which are strictly larger than the corresponding canonical stars. Moreover we present a family of counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ without restricting the number of parts.
item.dc:creator: Yury Person, Thomas Schweser

item.title: A refinement of the edge theorem for order and chain polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.07413v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite poset, we partition the edges of the order polytope and of the chain polytope into classes indexed by the connected convex subsets of the poset, and we establish that corresponding classes have the same cardinality. This yields a closed formula for the common number of edges, and it identifies the bijection of Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama as a disjoint union of simple bijections between corresponding classes, explaining why it is a bijection and how it acts on edge directions and lengths. As consequences, the two polytopes have equally many edge directions, with matching multiplicities, and, for every m, equally many pairs of vertices whose symmetric difference has m components; the chain polytope has at least as many edges parallel to each coordinate subspace as the order polytope; and the edge lengths of the chain polytope are dominated by those of the order polytope, with strict inequality in the last two comparisons exactly when the poset contains a three-element chain. We discuss implications for linear and convex combinatorial optimization over ideals and antichains. We also express the number of edges in terms of the comparability graph, extending to stable-set polytopes of all graphs; give a recursion for series-parallel posets and closed formulas for layered, zigzag and crown posets; and characterize the distributive lattices for which the two polytopes are unimodularly equivalent. Finally, either diameter can exceed the other arbitrarily; both are bounded by the width, and they coincide for series-parallel, zigzag and crown posets.
item.dc:creator: Jon Lee

item.title: A Spanning Subgraph of Conway's 99-graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.16266v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that in any hypothetical $G$ = srg(99,14,1,2) a spanning subgraph with $189$ edges is forced. Moreover, the graph formed out of the remaining edges has the spectrum $(12^1,-4^{30}, 3^{40},-2^6,0^7)$ expressed in Brouwer's notation.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Natal, Oleksiy Al-saadi

item.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $\Gamma$ satisfies $\exp(\Gamma) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Enami, Takahiro Matsushita

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.22909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$, even when both graphs have maximum degree at most three. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.
item.dc:creator: Jianshen Zhu

item.title: Inverse Zero-Sum Problems of Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant: Property C and Property D conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.25271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$.
