Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We prove that, for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n\ge2$, each of these properties holds if and only if $n$ is a power of two. This gives negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai Open Problems 1.2{GHST} in 2007, and disproves the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger [Conjecture 7.2]{GG} in 2006.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng

item.title: Quasirandomness from balanced and repeated subgraph counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.28124v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a graph on $m$ vertices with at least one edge, and let $0<p\le1$. We study when prescribed subgraph counts across disjoint vertex classes characterize $p$-quasirandom graph sequences. For positive multiplicities $\bm=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$ summing to $m$ and positive class proportions $\balpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)$ with total at most one, we first classify symmetrized repeated-class counts for $r\ge3$: when $0<p<1$, they are forcing precisely if $e(F)>1$ or $\balpha\ne\bm/m$. We also obtain a complete classification of labelled transversal counts: for \rev{$0<p<1$, the only nonforcing profile is $F=K_2$ with class proportions $(1/2,1/2)$.} Together, these results settle conjectures of Janson and S\'os [European J. Combin. 46 (2015)], Hatami, Hatami and Li [European J. Combin. 56 (2016)], and Janson [arXiv:2606.20186v1 (2026)]. The common ingredient is a balanced-count theorem for every graph with more than one edge, proved through a degree-sequence inequality, and its consequence of additive rigidity. Our arguments also determine the bad indices of the associated functional nullspaces and isolate the exceptional single-edge profiles. In particular, a non-divisibility theorem for grouped elementary symmetric polynomials excludes the higher-order obstructions in the repeated-class setting. In contrast, for two repeated classes and every $p\in(0,1)$, we construct nonquasirandom graph sequences satisfying the crossing-triangle counts at proportions $(1/3,2/3)$, with limiting edge density strictly below $p$. These counterexamples answer the crossing-triangle question negatively and show why the three-class assumption cannot be omitted.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

item.title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.28536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.
item.dc:creator: Jifu Lin, Heng Yang

item.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.32192v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid 3.12.12, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid 4.8.8, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid 3.6.3.6, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid 4.6.12, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid 3.4.6.4, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.
item.dc:creator: Rudini Sampaio

item.title: The Tur\'an number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Gy\H{o}ri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number of edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path. We consider the setting in which the host hypergraph is connected. Let $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{conn}}_r(n,\mathcal{BP}_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex, $r$-uniform, connected hypergraph that does not contain a Berge path on $k$ vertices. This number was determined by Zhang, Broersma, Gy\H{o}ri, Tompkins, Wang for $k \leq r+2$, and Zhao, Gerbner, Zhou for $k \geq 2r+2$. In this paper, we resolved the remaining cases $r+3 \leq k \leq 2r+1$ when $n$ is sufficiently large, confirming a conjecture of Zhang, et al.
item.dc:creator: Yupei Li, Ruth Luo

item.title: Which Schubert varieties are local complete intersections?
item.description: arXiv:1111.6146v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize by pattern avoidance the Schubert varieties for GL_n which are local complete intersections (lci). For those Schubert varieties which are local complete intersections, we give an explicit minimal set of equations cutting out their neighborhoods at the identity. Although the statement of our characterization only requires ordinary pattern avoidance, showing that the Schubert varieties not satisfying our conditions are not lci appears to require more general notions of pattern avoidance. The Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, originally introduced by Gasharov and Reiner, turn out to be an important subclass, and we further develop some of their combinatorics. Applications include formulas for Kostant polynomials and presentations of cohomology rings for lci Schubert varieties.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 107 (2013) 1004-1052
item.dc:creator: Henning \'Ulfarsson, Alexander Woo

item.title: On the Number of Circuits in Regular Matroids (with Connections to Lattices and Codes)
item.description: arXiv:1807.05164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for any regular matroid on $m$ elements and any $\alpha \geq 1$, the number of $\alpha$-minimum circuits, or circuits whose size is at most an $\alpha$-multiple of the minimum size of a circuit in the matroid is bounded by $m^{O(\alpha^2)}$. This generalizes a result of Karger for the number of $\alpha$-minimum cuts in a graph. As a consequence, we obtain similar bounds on the number of $\alpha$-shortest vectors in "totally unimodular" lattices and on the number of $\alpha$-minimum weight codewords in "regular" codes.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Gurjar, Nisheeth K. Vishnoi

item.title: On the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$
item.description: arXiv:2307.01819v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $g\ge 2$ and $n\ge 0$, let $\mathcal{H}_{g,n}\subset \mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ denote the complex moduli stack of $n$-marked smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$. A normal crossings compactification of this space is provided by the theory of pointed admissible $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-covers. We explicitly determine the resulting dual complex, and we use this to define a graph complex which computes the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. Using this graph complex, we give a sum-over-graphs formula for the $S_n$-equivariant weight zero compactly supported Euler characteristic of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. This formula allows for the computer-aided calculation, for each $g\le 7$, of the generating function $\mathsf{h}_g$ for these equivariant Euler characteristics for all $n$. More generally, we determine the dual complex of the boundary in any moduli space of pointed admissible $G$-covers of genus zero curves, when $G$ is a cyclic group of prime order, as a symmetric $\Delta$-complex. We use these complexes to generalize our formula for $\mathsf{h}_g$ to moduli spaces of $n$-pointed smooth prime cyclic covers of genus zero curves. This version contains corrections to the published version: see the attached erratum.
item.dc:creator: Madeline Brandt, Melody Chan, Siddarth Kannan

item.title: Rational Cherednik algebras and torus knot Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2402.18770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The HOMFLY polynomial of the $(m,n)$ torus knot $T_{m,n}$ can be extracted from the doubly graded character of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the type $A_{n-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra as observed by Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. It is furthermore conjectured that one can obtain the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of $T_{m,n}$ by considering a certain filtration on $L_{m/n}$. In this paper, we show that two of the proposed candidates, the algebraic filtration and the inductive filtration, are equal.
item.dc:creator: Xinchun Ma

item.title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2407.00971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Negu\c{t}: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.
item.dc:creator: Xinchun Ma

item.title: Characters of symmetric groups: sharp bounds on virtual degrees and the Witten zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2411.04347v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the virtual degrees introduced by Larsen and Shalev. This leads to improved bounds on characters of symmetric groups. We then sharpen bounds of Liebeck and Shalev concerning the Witten zeta function. Our main application is a characterization of the fixed-point free conjugacy classes whose associated random walk mixes in 2 steps.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Teyssier, Paul Th\'evenin

item.title: Forbidden Patterns in Mixed Linear Layouts
item.description: arXiv:2412.12786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An ordered graph is a graph with a total order over its vertices. A linear layout of an ordered graph is a partition of the edges into sets of either non-crossing edges, called stacks, or non-nesting edges, called queues. The stack (queue) number of an ordered graph is the minimum number of required stacks (queues). Mixed linear layouts combine these layouts by allowing each set of edges to form either a stack or a queue. The minimum number of stacks plus queues is called the mixed page number. It is well known that ordered graphs with small stack number are characterized, up to a function, by the absence of large twists (that is, pairwise crossing edges). Similarly, ordered graphs with small queue number are characterized by the absence of large rainbows (that is, pairwise nesting edges). However, no such characterization via forbidden patterns is known for mixed linear layouts. We address this gap by introducing patterns similar to twists and rainbows, which we call thick patterns; such patterns allow a characterization, again up to a function, of mixed linear layouts of bounded-degree graphs. That is, we show that a family of ordered graphs with bounded maximum degree has bounded mixed page number if and only if the size of the largest thick pattern is bounded. In addition, we investigate an exact characterization of ordered graphs whose mixed page number equals a fixed integer $ k $ via a finite set of forbidden patterns. We show that for every $ k \ge 2 $, there is no such characterization, which supports the nature of our first result.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Haun, Laura Merker, Sergey Pupyrev

item.title: Asymptotic coefficients of Weil-Petersson volumes in the large genus
item.description: arXiv:2501.06421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mirzakhani-Zograf proved the large genus asymptotic expansions of Weil-Petersson volumes and showed that the asymptotic coefficients are polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2},\pi^2]$. They also conjectured that these are actually polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2}]$. In this paper, we prove Mirzakhani-Zograf's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Huang

item.title: The Integrable Snake Model
item.description: arXiv:2501.15483v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A pure snake configuration is a bijection $\sigma:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing no two-cycles and such that for each $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ we have $\sigma(x) \in \{ x , x+ \mathbf{e}^1, x+\mathbf{e}^2 , x- \mathbf{e}^2 \}.$ The non-trivial cycles of a pure snake configuration may be regarded as a collection of non-intersecting paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that may travel right, up, or down (but not left) from a given vertex. Pure snake configurations are a generalisation of lozenge tilings, which are in natural correspondence with paths that only travel right or up. We introduce a partition function on a finite version of this model and study the probabilistic properties of random pure snake configurations chosen according to their contribution to this partition function. Under a suitable weighting, the model is integrable in the sense that we have access to explicit formulas for its partition function and correlation function. We utilise the integrable structure of this model in several applications through its various scaling limits, such as to prove a traffic representation of ASEP on the ring, generalising the analogous result for TASEP by the first author.
item.dc:creator: Samuel G. G. Johnston, Rohan Shiatis

item.title: A note on toric ideals of graphs and Knutson-Miller-Yong decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2502.08069v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use a Gr\"obner basis technique first introduced by Knutson, Miller and Yong to study the interplay between properties of a graph $G$ and algebraic properties of the toric ideal that it defines. We first recover a well-known height formula for the toric ideal of a graph $I_G$ and demonstrate an algebraic property that can detect when a graph deletion is bipartite. We also bound the chromatic number $\chi(G)$ using information about an initial ideal of $I_G$.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Da Silva, Emma Naguit, Jenna Rajchgot

item.title: Modeling FO-limits for monadically stable sequences
item.description: arXiv:2508.08960v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that given a monadically stable theory $T$, a sufficiently saturated $\mathbf M \models T$, and a coherent system of probability measures on the $\sigma$-algebras generated by parameter-definable sets of $\mathbf M$ in each dimension, we may produce a totally Borel $\mathbf B \prec \mathbf M$ realizing these measures. Our main application is to prove that every FO-convergent sequence of structures (with countable signature) from a monadically stable class admits a modeling limit. As another consequence, we prove a Borel removal lemma for monadically stable Lebesgue relational structures.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Braunfeld, Jaroslav Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, Patrice Ossona de Mendez

item.title: Freidel-Maillet type equations on fused K-matrices over the positive part of $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$
item.description: arXiv:2512.00819v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The positive part $U_q^+$ of the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ has a reflection equation presentation of Freidel-Maillet type (Baseilhac 2022). Its defining K-matrix has size $2 \times 2$ and can be expressed, using Rosso's embedding of $U_q^+$ into a $q$-shuffle algebra, as generating functions whose coefficients are Terwilliger's alternating PBW basis elements. This and older PBW bases of $U_q^+$ due to Damiani and Beck are unified by linear combinations of Catalan words (Ruan 2025). In this paper, we use this unification to define K-operators of any dimension $\geq 2$ in matrix form; the entries are explicit generating functions over $U_q^+$. Our main result is that any pair of such K-matrices, possibly of different dimensions, satisfy a Freidel-Maillet type equation. This yields a family of algebraic relations over $U_q^+$ that generalize Baseilhac's equation and can be used to study integrable systems or higher-spin representations. We conjecture that, for every spin, these K-matrices coincide with Lusztig's quasi R-matrix evaluated with its first leg on the corresponding finite-dimensional irreducible module.
item.dc:creator: Chenwei Ruan

item.title: Symbolic Integration of Differential Forms: From Abel to Zeilberger
item.description: arXiv:2601.00721v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper focuses on symbolic integration of differential forms, with a particular emphasis on historical and modern developments, from Abel's addition theorems for Abelian integrals to Zeilberger's creative telescoping for parameterized integrals. It explores closed rational $p$-forms and provides algorithmic approaches for their integration, extending classical results like Hermite reduction and Liouville's theorem. The integration of closed differential forms with parameters is further examined through telescopers, offering a unified framework for handling both algebraic and transcendental cases.
item.dc:creator: Shaoshi Chen, David A. Cox, Yisen Wang

item.title: Failing to keep the balance: explicit formulae and topological recursion for leaky Hurwitz numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.06094v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently a new family of enumerative invariants called leaky Hurwitz numbers was introduced by Cavalieri-Markwig-Ranganathan in the context of logarithmic intersection theory. They admit an interpretation via tropical covers where the balancing condition fails. We employ tropical geometry to prove a generalisation of the piecewise polynomiality of Accadia-Karev-Lewanski for leaky completed cycles Hurwitz numbers, and a different wall crossing that is cubic instead of quadratic. Using tropical combinatorics and generatingfunctionology, we also find closed formulae for one-part and two-part completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers in genus $0$. Working more generally with a view towards topological recursion, we use Hamiltonian flows to associate spectral curves to very general cut-and-join operators. Under mild analytic constraints, we find the appropriate spectral curves, and in case the leakiness is fixed, we show that the resulting enumerative invariants satisfy topological recursion. This provides a partial inverse to recent work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin producing differentials satisfying topological recursion for KP $\tau$-functions. In particular these results specialise to completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Anas Hahn, Reinier Kramer

item.title: On the Architectural Complexity of Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.04325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a unified theoretical framework for the rigorous analysis and systematic construction of deep neural networks (DNNs). This framework addresses a gap in existing theory by explicitly modeling the structure of tensor operations -- lower level information that is often abstracted. Our framework enables two novel objectives: (1) analysis of the evolution of architectural complexity over deep learning history, and (2) automatic construction of novel architectures based on new types of tensor operations. Our study of DNNs introduced over the past 40 years reveals a connection between groundbreaking architectures and increases in different types of architectural complexity. Moreover, we identify several large classes of higher complexity architectures that have not yet been explored. We then collect a dataset of 3,000+ higher complexity architectures, which we publicly release at: https://github.com/combinatoriallabs/ArchitecturalComplexity.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas J. Cooper, Fran\c{c}ois G. Meyer, Michael L. Roberts, Carlos Zapata-Carratal\'a, Lijun Chen, Danna Gurari

item.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
item.description: arXiv:2607.17469v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $\nu$ satisfying $\nu[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the random tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth, a tree max-flow/min-cut identity that makes worst-case survival probabilities exact and optimizable over the algorithm's choices. Three applications follow. For $n$ tasks on one machine, each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set, every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-\Theta(n)]$; a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment that satisfies a majority of each clause, we determine the sharp source threshold $s_*$. Below $s_*$, on some instances a single admissible source forces nontermination however clauses are selected; at $s_*$, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial Hamming distance, against linear under independence, with matching worst-case instances; and any fixed margin above $s_*$ restores linear dependence on the distance. Third, verified backtracking for noisy predecessor search remains correct under a sufficiently strong bound on the comparison errors. In every setting the algorithm may also restart, which supplies no fresh randomness; restarting restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.
item.dc:creator: Yunbei Xu

item.title: Average-Radius List-Decodability of Random Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2608.22663v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every prime power $q$ and every $p \in (0, 1-1/q)$, a random $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code of rate $1 - h_q(p) - \epsilon$ is $(p, C_{p,q}/\epsilon)$-average-radius list-decodable with probability at least $1 - q^{-\Omega(n)}$, i.e., for every center $y \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, the $C_{p,q}/\epsilon$ codewords closest to $y$ have average fractional Hamming distance at least $p$ from $y$. This extends a similar result for (standard) list-decoding due to Guruswami, H\r{a}stad, and Kopparty (2010) to the stronger average-radius guarantee, with the same $O(1/\epsilon)$ list size. For average-radius list-decoding, such a result was previously known only for binary linear codes (Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas, and Wootters, 2021) and for general (non-linear) random codes over arbitrary alphabets (Elias, 1991).
item.dc:creator: Venkatesan Guruswami, Shilun Li, Mihir Singhal

item.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
item.description: arXiv:2609.03532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every $\beta>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $\beta$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_\beta$ process for $\beta\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $\beta$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $\beta=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Xu

item.title: Minimum Cardinalities of Multipartite Unextendible Product Bases
item.description: arXiv:2609.05657v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In quantum information theory, the state space of a multipartite quantum system is modeled by a tensor product. In the tensor-product space $\C^{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\C^{d_p}$, a nonzero vector is a \emph{product state} if it can be written as $\ket{\varphi_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\ket{\varphi_p}$ with $\ket{\varphi_j}\in\C^{d_j}\setminus\{0\}$. An \emph{unextendible product basis} (UPB) is a finite family of pairwise orthogonal product states such that no nonzero product state is orthogonal to all of them. UPBs play a key role in investigating quantum entanglement and nonlocal phenomena. Finding a smallest UPB is a natural extremal problem: it asks how few pairwise orthogonal product states suffice to prevent any further product state from being added. The general minimum-size problem for UPBs has been studied for over two decades since the seminal work of Alon and Lov\'asz. Let $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)$ be the minimum cardinality of a UPB in the space, and let \(f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{p}(d_j-1)\) be the natural lower bound. Alon and Lov\'asz determined exactly when \(f_m\) attains the lower bound \(f_{LB}\), but the obstructed multipartite cases remained open in general. We prove a stabilization theorem: for every non-all-qubit system with $p\ge3$, whenever the natural lower bound $f_{LB}$ is unattainable, the true minimum is exactly $f_{LB}+1$. Precisely, if the number of even local dimensions $d_i$ is positive and even, and at least one local dimension is greater than two, then \(f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)+1\). The proof is built on a unified graph-theoretic framework. Our result, together with earlier work, settles the minimum size problem for UPBs in all finite quantum systems.

item.title: Internal congruences modulo powers of 2 for $k$-colored overpartitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2609.11806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\overline{po}_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-colored overpartitions of $n$ into odd parts. For every odd number of colors, we establish infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $2$. The proof proceeds by expressing the relevant difference generating functions as a fixed theta quotient multiplied by polynomials in an auxiliary function. Uniform lower bounds for the $2$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients then yield the stated internal congruences. These results generalize an internal congruence of Saikia, Sarma and Sellers (J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.~2025) on overpartition triples into odd parts.

item.title: Finite-color reconstruction of groups and coherent configurations
item.description: arXiv:2609.33938v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every group has a canonical coloring of its unordered pairs by inverse pairs of differences. We prove that this coloring can be coarsened to four colors without changing its color-preserving permutation group, for groups of arbitrary cardinality. Four is the least uniform bound. A related construction applies to finite homogeneous coherent configurations: if every basic relation has valency at most $d$, where $d\geq 2$, a coarsening with at most $2d+1$ off-diagonal colors in the symmetric case, or $2d+3$ off-diagonal arc colors in general, has the original configuration as its coherent closure. Two-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman refinement recovers that partition within $2\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ rounds on $n$ points, with the specified atomic initialization. Affine-plane schemes show that linear dependence on valency is necessary. We apply the group realization to classify groups admitting naturalizing invariant metrics and show that, for a suitable such metric, naming the identity determines the compatible multiplication uniquely. Finally, using additional Cayley-realization and finite-classification inputs and explicit certificates, we determine the least number of metric values for every group. The direct universal construction and the finite coherent-reconstruction theorem do not depend on those computations.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
item.description: arXiv:2610.09258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=\tau\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $\tau\lambda_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $\lambda_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $\Delta\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $\delta>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.09972v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs. For every finite simple bipartite graph of maximum degree at most an integer $\Delta\ge3$, the algorithm assigns signs to its edges so that the signed adjacency matrix has operator norm strictly less than $2\sqrt{\Delta-1}$. Our algorithm builds on the randomized recursive repair framework of Jadbabaie, Saberi, and Sra~\cite{JSS26}, with deterministic rules for sign selection and vertex deletion.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqiang Xu

item.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26737v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $\delta \in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_\delta((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley, David Chew
